drills.q: Put 食べる (to eat) into polite present ます-form.
drills.hint: Ichidan verb: drop る, add ます. Romaji: tabemasu.

drills.q: Put 行く (to go) into polite past.
drills.hint: Godan: 行き + ました. Romaji: ikimashita.

drills.q: Give the て-form of 飲む (to drink).
drills.hint: む/ぶ/ぬ verbs take んで. Romaji: nonde.

drills.q: Give the polite negative of 話す (to speak): 'do not speak'.
drills.hint: Stem 話し + ません. Romaji: hanashimasen.

drills.q: Put する (to do) into polite past.
drills.hint: する is irregular: し + ました. Romaji: shimashita.

drills.q: Give the potential form (can eat) of 食べる.
drills.hint: Ichidan potential: drop る, add られる. Romaji: taberareru.

drills.q: How do you say 'water' in Japanese?
drills.hint: Romaji: mizu; note 湯 (yu) is hot water.

drills.q: How do you say 'station' in Japanese?
drills.hint: Romaji: eki.

drills.q: What is the Japanese word for 'friend'?
drills.hint: Romaji: tomodachi.

drills.q: How do you say 'delicious' (い-adjective) in Japanese?
drills.hint: Romaji: oishii; casual うまい umai.

drills.q: What is the Japanese word for 'tomorrow'?
drills.hint: Romaji: ashita (or asu, more formal).

drills.q: Fill in the particle: 私___学生です (As for me, I'm a student).
drills.hint: Topic marker は, pronounced 'wa'.

drills.q: Fill in the particle for the direct object: パン___食べます (I eat bread).
drills.hint: を marks the direct object; pronounced 'o'.

drills.q: Fill in the particle: 東京___行きます (I go to Tokyo).
drills.hint: に (or へ) marks destination; へ is read 'e'.

drills.q: Fill in the particle for place of action: 図書館___勉強します (I study at the library).
drills.hint: で marks where an action occurs.

drills.q: How do you say the number 8 in Japanese (kanji)?
drills.hint: Romaji: hachi.

drills.q: How do you say '3 o'clock' in Japanese?
drills.hint: Number + 時 (ji). Romaji: sanji.

drills.q: How do you say 'Thank you' politely in Japanese?
drills.a: ありがとうございます
drills.hint: Romaji: arigatō gozaimasu.

drills.q: How do you say 'Excuse me / I'm sorry' (all-purpose) in Japanese?
drills.hint: Romaji: sumimasen; also used to get attention.

drills.q: How do you ask 'How much is it?' in Japanese?
drills.hint: Romaji: ikura desu ka.
